1944-1960

Caption This

The Cold War and the Affluent Fifties

17

How this works (15–20 minutes)

  1. Look at each of the 5 images. Read the “What you’re looking at” line.
  2. Write a short, funny caption, like a meme. Pick a caption style if you want one.
  3. Then write 2–3 sentences about what is really going on. Use at least one key term from the lesson. Type the key term in English, exactly as shown.
  4. Save Progress any time. When all 5 are done, press Finished and upload the file to Canvas.

Keep it respectful: make the joke about the company, the idea, or the situation. Never joke about workers, children, immigrants, enslaved or freed people, Native peoples, anyone’s race or religion, or people who were hurt.

“All Our Colors to the Mast”

Not done

What you’re looking at: A poster from Norton Ch. 25. A big sailing ship has flags of many countries for sails. The word EUROPA is on the ship’s side above white waves. Norton says thirteen European nations held a poster contest in 1950 as part of the Marshall Plan. This poster, by Dutch artist Reyn Dirksen, won.

Heads up: This poster is about countries working together. Aim your joke at the ship, the flags, or the crowded sails. Never joke about any country’s people or about any group.

  • Look at the sails. What are they made of? What do the flags say about the countries?
  • Read the big word on the ship. What does the poster want the countries to do together?
Pick a caption style (optional)

Key terms that fit this image: Marshall Plan (1948)containment
Image 2 of 5

Veterans job-training poster

Not done

What you’re looking at: A poster with a black-and-white photo and a red bar at the bottom. The top says, “Veterans — earn while you learn thru ON-THE-JOB TRAINING.” Two men stand at a big saw in a workshop. The younger man guides a board through the saw. The older man, in glasses and suspenders, points toward the board. The red bar says to ask your nearest Veterans Administration office.

Heads up: This poster was made to help veterans find work. Aim your joke at the saw, the slogan, or the idea of learning on the job. Never joke about the two men, about veterans, or about anyone who served.

  • Read the slogan at the top. What does “earn while you learn” promise a veteran?
  • Look at the two men and the saw. What kind of training is the poster showing?
Pick a caption style (optional)

Key terms that fit this image: GI Bill of Rights (1944)baby boom
Image 3 of 5

“Dewey Defeats Truman”

Not done

What you’re looking at: A black-and-white photograph from Norton Ch. 25. A smiling man in round glasses holds up a newspaper with both hands. The big headline says “DEWEY DEFEATS TRUMAN.” The paper is the Chicago Daily Tribune. Norton says this early edition was wrong. President Truman won the 1948 election.

Heads up: This is a famous newspaper mistake. Aim your joke at the headline, the newspaper, or the election polls. Never joke about how anyone looks or about any group of voters.

  • Read the headline. Then think about who really won. Why might the newspaper get it wrong?
  • Look at the smile on the man holding the paper. How does he feel about the headline?
Pick a caption style (optional)

Key terms that fit this image: Fair Deal (1949)Dixiecrats
Image 4 of 5

“Firing of MacArthur” cartoon

Not done

What you’re looking at: A color political cartoon from Norton Ch. 25. Three men sweat and hop in a huge frying pan labeled “Firing of MacArthur.” Their jackets are marked H.S.T., State Dept., and Pentagon. A hand marked “John Q.” holds the pan over a gas flame. The gas hose is labeled “Public Opinion.”

Heads up: This cartoon is about a big argument in the government during the Korean War. Aim your joke at the frying pan, the flame, or the sweating. Never joke about how the men look, or about the soldiers who fought and died in Korea.

  • Read the labels on the three men and on the pan. Who is in the hot seat, and why?
  • Read the label on the gas hose. Who is turning up the heat?
Pick a caption style (optional)

Key terms that fit this image: containmentNSC-68
Image 5 of 5

McCarthy and the broom

Not done

What you’re looking at: A black-and-white photograph from Norton Ch. 25. A man in a long coat stands on a stone ledge and holds a very tall broom with a striped handle. The big dome of the U.S. Capitol rises behind him. Norton says this 1954 photo shows Senator Joseph R. McCarthy, who said he would “sweep” Communists out of the federal government and beyond.

Heads up: This is a serious one. During the Red Scare, many people lost their jobs and good names because of accusations. Write one clear line. No jokes about anyone who was accused, and no jokes about the people in the photo. Look at the broom, the dome, and the pose.

  • Look at the broom. What does Senator McCarthy say he is going to sweep out?
  • Look at the Capitol dome behind him. Why might he pose in front of it?
Pick a caption style (optional)

Key terms that fit this image: McCarthyismHouse Committee on Un-American Activities (HUAC)
